quests.instruction: Which solid shape has no flat faces anywhere, just one smooth curved surface?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape that rolls freely in every single direction.
quests.explanation: A sphere has zero flat faces — its entire surface is one smooth curve.
quests.funFact: Because it has no flat parts, a sphere can never sit still on its own unless something stops it.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has exactly 6 flat faces, and every single one is a square?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape where turning it any way still shows a square face.
quests.explanation: A cube has 6 flat faces, and every one of them is a perfect square.
quests.funFact: Because all its faces are equal squares, a cube looks the same from many different angles.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved surface joining them?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with a flat top, a flat bottom, and a curved middle.
quests.explanation: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces on top and bottom, joined by 1 curved surface.
quests.funFact: A cylinder can roll along its curved side, but it stands still on its flat circle ends.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has exactly 1 flat circle face and 1 curved surface that comes to a point?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with only one flat side, opposite a pointed tip.
quests.explanation: A cone has just 1 flat circle face at the bottom and 1 curved surface rising to a point.
quests.funFact: A cone's single point is called its apex, sitting directly above the center of its circle base.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has a flat polygon base with triangle faces meeting at one top point?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with slanted triangle sides all meeting at a single peak.
quests.explanation: A pyramid has a flat base with triangle faces that all meet together at one top point.
quests.funFact: Every triangle face of a pyramid shares that same single top point, called the apex.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 6 flat rectangle faces, but they are not all required to be square?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape like a stretched cube, with longer and shorter faces.
quests.explanation: A rectangular prism has 6 flat rectangle faces, and unlike a cube, they don't all have to be square.
quests.funFact: Every cube is technically a rectangular prism, but not every rectangular prism is a cube.

quests.instruction: If you look straight down at the flat bottom of a cone, what flat shape do you see?
quests.hint: Think about the shape of a cone's one and only flat face.
quests.explanation: Looking straight at a cone's flat face shows a circle, since that face is perfectly round.
quests.funFact: A cone is basically a circle with a curved surface rising up to a point.

quests.instruction: If you look straight at one face of a cube, what flat shape do you see?
quests.hint: Think about the shape of any single face on a die.
quests.explanation: Looking straight at any face of a cube shows a square, since all its faces are equal squares.
quests.funFact: A cube is made entirely of 6 matching square faces.

quests.instruction: If you look straight at one slanted side of a pyramid, what flat shape do you usually see?
quests.hint: Think about the shape of the slanted faces leading up to a pyramid's point.
quests.explanation: Looking straight at a pyramid's slanted side usually shows a triangle, since those faces meet at a point.
quests.funFact: A pyramid's triangle sides are what give it that classic pointed look.

quests.instruction: If you look straight at the long side of a rectangular prism, what flat shape do you usually see?
quests.hint: Think about the shape of the long flat side of a tissue box.
quests.explanation: Looking straight at the long side of a rectangular prism usually shows a rectangle.
quests.funFact: A rectangular prism's faces can be a mix of rectangles, and sometimes squares too.

quests.instruction: If you look straight at one flat end of a cylinder, what flat shape do you see?
quests.hint: Think about the shape of the flat top of a soup can.
quests.explanation: Looking straight at either flat end of a cylinder shows a circle.
quests.funFact: A cylinder's two circle ends are always exactly the same size as each other.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape looks exactly the same as a circle from absolutely every single angle?
quests.hint: Think of the only solid shape with no flat sides at all, viewed from any direction.
quests.explanation: A sphere looks like a circle outline from every single angle, since it's perfectly round in 3D.
quests.funFact: You could turn a sphere any way at all, and its outline would always look like a circle.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 8 corners, where 3 flat square faces meet at each one?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape where every corner is shared by exactly 3 square faces.
quests.explanation: A cube has 8 corners, and exactly 3 square faces meet together at each one.
quests.funFact: Counting a cube's corners is a fun way to notice how its faces connect to each other.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape also has 8 corners, just like a cube, but its faces aren't all squares?
quests.hint: Think of the stretched-out cousin of a cube, with the same number of corners.
quests.explanation: A rectangular prism has 8 corners just like a cube, but its faces are rectangles instead of all squares.
quests.funFact: Cubes and rectangular prisms share the same corner count because they're such close shape cousins.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape (with a square base) has 5 corners — 4 around the base and 1 at the top point?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with one extra special corner high above its base.
quests.explanation: A pyramid with a square base has 5 corners: 4 around the base and 1 at the top point.
quests.funFact: That top corner is called the apex, and every triangle face touches it.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has just 1 corner, sitting at the very top of its pointed tip?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with the fewest corners of all — just a single point.
quests.explanation: A cone has only 1 corner, located at the very tip of its point.
quests.funFact: That single pointed corner on a cone is also called its apex.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has zero corners and zero edges anywhere on its surface?
quests.hint: Think of the roundest solid shape, with nothing but curve.
quests.explanation: A sphere has zero corners and zero edges — its whole surface is one smooth curve.
quests.funFact: Having no edges or corners is exactly why a sphere rolls so smoothly.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has zero corners, but 2 curved edges where its flat ends meet its curved side?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with two circular edges but no sharp points anywhere.
quests.explanation: A cylinder has zero corners, but it does have 2 curved edges where the flat ends meet the curved side.
quests.funFact: Even though a cylinder has curved edges, it has no sharp corners at all.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 12 edges, all of them exactly the same length?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape where every straight edge you could measure comes out equal.
quests.explanation: A cube has 12 edges, and every single one is exactly the same length.
quests.funFact: Having equal edges is part of what makes a cube such a balanced, sturdy shape.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 12 edges, just like a cube, but the edges come in different lengths?
quests.hint: Think of the stretched cousin of a cube with the same edge count, but not all equal.
quests.explanation: A rectangular prism has 12 edges just like a cube, but they come in different lengths depending on the box.
quests.funFact: This is one more way rectangular prisms and cubes are closely related shapes.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape (with a square base) has 8 edges — 4 around the base and 4 rising to the top point?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with edges both around its base and slanting up to a peak.
quests.explanation: A pyramid with a square base has 8 edges: 4 forming the base and 4 rising up to the top point.
quests.funFact: The 4 slanted edges of a pyramid all meet together at the very same top corner.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape can never be stacked on top of another one without rolling away?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with absolutely no flat surface to rest on.
quests.explanation: A sphere has no flat surface at all, so stacking one directly on another makes it roll right off.
quests.funFact: That's why balls need a special rack or bowl instead of being stacked like boxes.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape is the easiest to stack neatly because every face is a flat, equal square?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape whose matching flat faces make stacking simple.
quests.explanation: A cube's equal flat square faces make it very easy to stack neatly in any direction.
quests.funFact: Building blocks are often cube-shaped exactly because they stack so easily.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape can either roll along its side or stand still on one of its flat circle ends?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape that behaves differently depending on which side is down.
quests.explanation: A cylinder can roll along its curved side, but it stands perfectly still on its flat circle ends.
quests.funFact: That's why cans are stored standing up, but sometimes roll if tipped on their side.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape can rock back and forth on its curved side, but not roll away completely?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape whose pointed tip keeps it from rolling in a straight line.
quests.explanation: A cone can rock or spin around its point, since its shape prevents it from rolling straight.
quests.funFact: If you nudge a cone lying on its side, it actually rolls in a circle instead of a straight line.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape sits solidly on its flat base and would never roll at all?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with a wide, heavy base and no curved parts.
quests.explanation: A pyramid rests firmly on its flat base and, with no curved parts, it never rolls.
quests.funFact: This is part of why ancient pyramid buildings have stayed standing for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape, like a cube, always sits flat and stable no matter which face is down?
quests.hint: Think of the box-shaped solid that never rolls, no matter how you set it down.
quests.explanation: A rectangular prism sits flat and stable on any of its 6 rectangle faces.
quests.funFact: This is exactly why boxes are so easy to stack and store in any direction.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has a surface where every single point is the same distance from the center?
quests.hint: Think of the solid version of a circle, round in three dimensions instead of two.
quests.explanation: Every point on a sphere's surface is the exact same distance from its center point.
quests.funFact: This equal-distance rule is exactly why a sphere is sometimes called a 3D circle.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape is like a square that has been given equal depth in every direction?
quests.hint: Think of the solid version of a square, deep in three dimensions instead of flat.
quests.explanation: A cube is like a square stretched with equal depth in every direction, making all 6 faces squares.
quests.funFact: This is why a cube is sometimes described as the solid version of a flat square.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape is like a rectangle that has been given depth, but not necessarily equal depth?
quests.hint: Think of the solid version of a rectangle, stretched into three dimensions.
quests.explanation: A rectangular prism is like a rectangle given depth, though that depth doesn't have to match the other sides.
quests.funFact: This is why a rectangular prism is sometimes described as the solid version of a flat rectangle.
